description:
Caltech Library maintains a list of people, groups and funders and their related identifiers. For many years these were managed using a spreadsheets. That has become cumbersome. **COLD** manages data as JSON objects in [dataset](https://github.com/caltechlibrary/dataset) collections.

**COLD** is implemented as three web web services

- cold web UI
- cold JSON API (provided by datasetd)
- cold reports (the report request system)

Reports are implemented as a set of programs or bash scripts.

TypeScript+Deno is used to implement the web UI and report system.
The JSON API is provided by Dataset's datasetd.
Access control is provided by the front end web server integrated with Shibboleth.
name: cold
releaseNotes:
- **The people push to RDM (cold#122, DR-0037 to DR-0041).** COLD can make the CaltechAUTHORS RDM names pick list match its people. COLD is authoritative: a full push writes every COLD person by clpid (create, update, revive a removed entry, replace a legacy one) and removes every entry COLD does not hold, so **a person deleted in COLD leaves the pick list at the next full push**; a push of one person writes that person only. There is no cap on removals, the metadata records are never written, and the default is a dry run (`PEOPLE_SYNC_MODE=apply` writes). A new page, `rdm_people_sync.html` ("Sync People to RDM", on the dashboard), shows where the next run will go, the latest run and what needs a person's attention, with **Sync all people now** and **Rerun for CLPID**; each person's page has a **Sync CLPID to RDM** button. A run is a report request (`run_people_sync` and `run_people_sync_person`), so cron and the buttons share one queue; `run_people_sync.bash` and `people_sync` do the work and `GET /rdm/people_sync/target` serves the page its next-run line.
- A person's affiliations come from COLD alone: the `ror` field plus Caltech and JPL from the two boxes, each once (DR-0040). ORCID, ISNI and ROR are validated with `idutils`; a value that does not validate is not pushed and is listed as a warning (DR-0041).
- Safeguards: an apply keeps a **pre-image** of the names tables on the RDM host before its first write, in `PEOPLE_SYNC_PREIMAGE_DIR` (default `/var/tmp/people_sync_preimages`, mode 700, the newest 20 kept), and records its path on the run; the run is refused if that directory cannot be made. One run at a time (a lock; exit 75). `PEOPLE_SYNC_STALE_SECONDS` (default 600) is the longest a run may take, enforced with `timeout` on the RDM host. An apply is refused on an RDM major version other than 13, and an empty or malformed people list is refused (exit 65).
- **Install with irdmtools v0.2.0.** The program that writes to RDM is `scripts/people_rdm_*.py` in irdmtools; `cold` ships it from `../irdmtools/scripts` on every run and records its hash on the run, so the two are released and installed together.
- **Upgrading a deployment:** create the two new collections, `dataset init people_sync_runs.ds` and `dataset init people_sync_items.ds`, and restart `cold_api`; write the target env file and set `PEOPLE_SYNC_ENV` for `cold`, `cold_reports` and cron (it has no default); rebuild `bin/people_sync`, since `run_people_sync.bash` prefers it. The release builds of `cold` now carry `--allow-env=PEOPLE_SYNC_ENV`; without it the page cannot name the next run's target. Start with a dry run from the command line and take a table dump of `name_metadata` before the first apply. See docs/rdm_people_push.md and docs/deployment.md.
- `load_collections.bash` no longer ignores failures: for each collection it clears then loads, passes `-max-capacity` (`MAX_CAPACITY`, default 8 MB) and checks the record count against the dump's line count, refuses to clear a non-empty collection from an empty dump unless `ALLOW_EMPTY=1`, and refuses to run while `datasetd` is running; a record over `dataset load`'s 1 MB buffer used to stop the load part way and still exit 0. `grab_production_collection_snapshots.bash` is a development wrapper that dumps the collections on `apps`, copies the zip here and loads it.
- New: the manual page `people_sync(1)`. `docs/deployment.md` states the minimums in `codemeta.json` (Deno 2.8.2, Dataset 2.5.1); it had older ones.
- Known limits: the page does not disable its button when it cannot read the next run's target, so do not press it until the target line names the instance you expect; nothing restores from the JSON-lines pre-image (the way back is a table dump taken before the first apply); a ROR's check digits are not verified; the site-wide `section` CSS rule overflows at 320 px.
